full_judgment:
4. In the plaint, it was stated, inter alia, that Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Mogbazar was born in village Bardhanpara, police station-Murar-e in the District of Birbhum in West Bengal of the then undivided India. Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Mogbazar, after passing engineering from Calcutta University in 1950 worked as site Engineer for 2(two) years under Messrs Bridge and Roof Company, India and then migrated to Dhaka and joined C&B Department in 1951 as an Assistant Engineer under the then Government of Pakistan. While serving in C&B department, Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Mogbazar purchased 10(ten) kathas of land at Bara Mogbazar by a registered deed dated 28- 9-1957 being deed No.9847. Subsequently, he by a registered hebanama dated 17-8-1979 being deed No.31901 transferred the said land of Bara Mogbazar to her wife, late Selima Begum, where- in a three storied building was constructed after obtaining plan from RAJUK. Engineer Humayun Reza resided at 157, Bara Mogbazar till his death on 2-2-2004. As Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza was the resident of 157, Bara Mogbazar, in all the Government papers including voter list and passport, his permanent address was mentioned as 157, Bara Mogbazar (hereinafter referred to as Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Mogbazar). Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Mogbazar, while serving in C & B, had gone to Canada for taking higher training in 1960 and after completing training, he came back to this Country and again joined C & B and was promoted as the Executive Engineer. At that time, the then Dacca Improvement Trust (DIT) now RAJUK published notice for allotment of plots at Gulshan Model Town for 99 years. Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Mogbazar applied for allotment of a plot therein and pursuant to his application, he was allotted plot No.34( old), I 13(new), Block-C WN(B) Gulshan Model Town, Gulshan (hereinafter referred to as the suit plot) vide allotment letter under Memo No.2409 dated 21-3-1962. Engineer Humayun Kabir Shamsul Reza of Bara Mogbazar paid the installments against the suit plot on 26-3-1962, 26-6-1962, 7-1-1963, 5-3- 1964 and 3-2-1966. The DIT delivered possession of the suit plot to him by a letter dated 1-8-1962. After getting possession of the allotted plot, Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Mogbazar created a boundary wall and also constructed a katcha room therein and started to possess the same by keeping a Caretaker. As per the prevailing system at the then DIT, two printed forms of the main lease deed were filled up for keeping one with DIT as lessor and the other for the lessee. The two lease deeds were signed by Abul Ehsan on behalf of the lessor (DIT) and the plaintiffs' father, Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Mogbazar, the lessee, on 1-8-1962. The serial numbers of two deeds were 7848 and 7849 respectively. Both deeds were registered in the same number being No.7198 and then deed No.7848 was given to the plaintiffs' father and the other deed being serial No.7849 was kept with the other documents in the file of the suit plot at DIT. The plaintiffs' father, Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Mogbazar, subsequently, had left the job of C & B and joined as Director in one of the company of Islam Group of Zahurul Islam, namely: Bengal Development Corporation. The plaintiffs' father constructed a building measuring 8,000 square feet in every floor (storey has not been mentioned) on the suit plot by obtaining a plan from RAJUK and taking loan from the House Building Finance Corporation by mortgaging the suit plot with it on 17-5-1967. Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Mogbazar mutated his name with the revenue department of the Government, opened Municipal holding in his name in respect of the suit plot and took connections of various utility services, such as: WASA, Electricity and Titas gas in his own name and paid tax, rents and bills accordingly. He had also let out the said building to different organizations and persons and lastly, it was let out to Aftab Multipurpose Firm Ltd. The names of the tenants are: (1) Agency for International Development, (2) Mr D Markiing and A Lippene ott., (3) Mr LLoye F Gonyea, (4) Mr MM Abouzeid of United Nations Development Programme, (5) Mr Fred HW. Petrini, (6) Sewdish International Service, (7) Dr Martin W. Bloem of Helen Keller International, (8) Uttara Bank Limited and (9) Aftab Bahumukhi Firm Limited. 

 The trial Court dismissed the suit on the findings, inter alia, that plaintiff, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, was not the original allottee, therefore, RAJUK could not give permission to him to sell the suit plot and that RAJUK recognized Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar as the allottee of the suit plot and also approved Eastern Housing Limited as his attorney; the plaintiff's suit was not maintainable. In coming to the said findings, the trial Court held that the suit plot was allotted to Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, who was the Executive Engineer of C&B and that RS khatian No.1174 in respect of the suit plot was recorded in the name of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar; plaintiff, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza as PW 1 in his cross-examination clearly stated that he never resided at 157, Bara Moghbazar and while he deposed, he was residing at 911/1 Shewrapara as a tenant of one Monowara; the suit plot was allotted to Executive Engineer, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza and admittedly the plaintiff was Diploma Engineer and therefore, it was not believable that he could join a big Department like C&B as Assistant Engineer in 1950/1952 and was promoted as the Executive Engineer in 1956/57 and therefore, it could not be accepted that the plaintiff got the allotment of the suit plot as Executive Engineer. The trial Court further noticed that PW 1 (Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza) admitted in his cross- examination that in 1965, he was a voter at Ishwardi and after liberation of Bangladesh, he participated in an election at Fulbaria under the district of Dinajpur, which was not believable, asit was not natural that a person, who served as an Executive Engineer, would go to an Upazila and participate in the election. The trial Court further observed that it was not natural that a person, who became the Executive Engineer, would live at Pabna, then at Dinajpur and then in Dhaka. The trial Court further observed that it was also not believable that a person, who got a plot from RAJUK at Gulshan, would reside at Ishwardi in the district of Pabna and then at Fulbaria in the district of Dinajpur. Although the plaintiff claimed that he accepted domicile certificate but that was not with him. The trial Court further observed that the plaintiff in his cross-examination admitted that though he served as an Executive Engineer in C&B, he did not open any bank account, which also proved that he was not an Executive Engineer, because the salary of a first class employee is given through cheque and in the absence of bank account, he could not draw his salary. The trial Court further noticed that the plaintiff admitted in his cross-examination that he had gone to India in 1958 and married his cousin (খালাতো বোন) at 'Arai' in India. The trial Court noticed that a person, who migrated to this country, in 1947 and was a high official in C&B, could not go to India without the permission of his office or the Government for marrying there. PW2, a guard of Sonali Bank, Motijheel Branch, was disbelieved by the trial Court on the ground that when the plaintiff admitted that he had no bank account, it was not believable that he would be acquainted with a guard of Sonali Bank. The trial Court also observed that it was not natural that the plaintiff, who claimed to be an Executive Engineer, would develop a relationship with a guard of a bank. The trial Court disbelieved PW 3 on the ground that he deposed that he got himself acquainted with the plaintiff through one of the relative, namely, Shamim; when PWI in his cross-examination admitted that he had no relative in this country. (PWs 2 and 3 were examined to prove plaintiff's possession in the suit plot.) The trial Court relied on the evidence of DW1, an official of RAJUK that no application was filed by the plaintiff, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, to RAJUK for permission to sell the suit plot to MNH Bulu and that no application was filed by the plaintiff to RAJUK on 18-2-2004 to sell the suit plot. The trial Court further held that RAJUK did not recognize the plaintiff of the instant suit as the allottee of the suit plot, rather RAJUK admitted Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar as the allottee and approved the power of attorney given by him to Eastern Housing Limited. 

 49. Title Suit No.l76 of 2004, giving rise to Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.2198 of 2011, was filed by one Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza impleading the officials of RAJUK only for two reliefs (i) that he was legally entitled to get the sale permission of the suit plot and the defendants were bound to issue such sale permission on receiving the proper transfer fees from him and (ii) that the defendants were bound to dispose of the application filed by him on 18-2-2004 for sale permission of the suit plot within a specified time as to be directed by the Court claiming himself to be the allottee of the suit plot. He claimed that he was an Executive Engineer of C&B under the Ministry of Communications. But in support of his said claim, he did not file a single paper. The trial Court considering the evidence on record, both oral and documentary, dismissed the suit on the clear findings, inter alia, that the suit plot was allotted to Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza who was the Executive Engineer of C&B ; the plaintiff was a Diploma Engineer and it was not believable that he could join a big department like C&B as an Assistant Engineer in 1950/1952 and then promoted as Executive Engineer in 1956/57 The trial Court further observed that the plaintiff in his cross-examination admitted that though he served as an Executive Engineer in C&B, he did not open any  bank account, which also proved that he was not an Executive Engineer, because the salary of a first class employee is given through cheque and in the  absence of bank account* he could not draw his  salary and that he was not the allottee of the suit allot. Therefore, RAJUK could not give permission to him to sell the suit plot. RAJUK recognized Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar as the allottee of the suit plot and also approved Eastern Housing Limited as his attorney and that the suit was not maintainable. The trial Court further held that the suit plot was allotted to Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, who was an Executive Engineer of C&B and RAJUK did not recognize the plaintiff as the allottee of the suit plot. RS Khatian  No.11174 in respect of the suit plot was recorded  in the name of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar and plaintiff Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza as PW1 in his cross-examination  clearly stated that he never resided at 157, Bara  Moghbazar and while he deposed, he was residing at 911/1 Shewrapara as a tenant of one Monowara. The trial Court further held that no application was filed to RAJUK by the plaintiff on 18-2-2004 for permission to sell the suit plot to MNH Bulu. While dismissing the first appeal, the learned Judges affirmed the said findings of the trial Court, but giving their own reasonings. The learned Judges gave further finding that the plaintiff did not produce any copy of his application filed to RAJUK for sale permission of the suit plot. The learned Judges taking into notice of the fact that RAJUK in its written statement stated that "such file in the name of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza as mentioned is not traceable in the office of RAJUK" concluded that "so, it may be legally presumed that such application was notified and alternatively it may be presumed that the suit plot was not allotted to the plaintiff." The learned Judges came to further finding that documents filed by the plaintiff exhibited in the suit clearly show that those were prepared in the name  of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar which was admittedly the permanent address of Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun  Reza, a different person. The learned Judges further held that the suit of the plaintiff for sale permission simpliciter was not maintainable as he himself admitted in the plaint as well as in his deposition that he was out of possession and that Title Suit No.81 of 2006 filed by the heirs of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar for declaration of title and permanent injunction heard simultaneously by the same Court (the plaintiff was defendant No.3 in the suit) was decreed. The learned Judges came to further finding that though PW I (Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza) claimed that he was an Executive  Engineer, but his testimony regarding Service  Book, ACR, and Organogram clearly proved that he was not a service holder at all. The findings given by the trial Court as well as the High Court Division as to the actual allottee of the suit plot are so specific and well reasoned that we see no scope of touching with those findings. More interesting thing is that the whole case of the plaintiff was that he filed an application to RAJUK on 18-2-2004 to give him permission to sell the suit plot to MNH Bulu, but that application was not disposed of by RAJUK, which gave him the cause of action to file the suit. And, in fact, the plaintiff prayed for a relief to give direction to RAJUK to dispose of his said application within certain specific time fixed by the Court, but no such application was filed before the Court. Thus, the very foundation of the plaintiff's case had no existence. So, the plaintiff was not entitled to get any relief in the suit. Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan and Mr AF Hasan Ariff, appearing for the petitioner, could not lay their hands on any of the material evidence on record to assail the findings jotted down hereinabove either on the ground of misreading or non-consideration of any material evidence by the Courts below and thus, term those as perverse. (The reasonings, given by the trial Court and the learned Judges of the High Court Division in coming to their findings have been exhaustively noted while summarizing their findings, so those are not repeated.)
